interpolation.note: Li et al. report 10–50 mL for a ~500–2,500 token inference query. Their MIT-licensed notebooks operate at datacenter-hour / training-run granularity (power × on-site WUE + off-site EWIF × PUE), not per token. The rates below are aqua-tokens' linear interpolation onto a 1,000-token reference (the midpoint of that query-size band), not a value the paper states directly. 1.2M tokens × 10–50 mL / 1,000 tokens = 12–60 L.

scope1plus2.label: scope-1+2
scope1plus2.description: On-site cooling plus electricity-generation water. Default: this is the range that matters.
sources: Li, P., Yang, J., Islam, M.A., Ren, S. Making AI Less Thirsty. UC Riverside, 2023 / Commun. ACM 2024. arXiv:2304.03271. 10–50 mL per ~500–2,500 token query; power-plant water can be up to 75% of the total.

scope1.label: scope-1
scope1.description: On-site cooling only. Conservative undercount: excludes electricity-generation water.
sources: Google 2025 Environmental Report (median Gemini prompt, on-site cooling).
Sam Altman, June 2025 disclosure (ChatGPT, on-site cooling).

caveat: Estimates vary 30x+ depending on scope, model version, query complexity, and data center location.
citation: Li, P., Yang, J., Islam, M.A., Ren, S. "Making AI Less Thirsty: Uncovering and Addressing the Secret Water Footprint of AI Models." UC Riverside, 2023 / Commun. ACM 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03271
